rows.why: Item 2 asks how a stored value is cleaned before matching, and that decides whether "Draft" or " PUBLISHED " reads as its status. The pick lowercases and trims, and the run shows "  Draft " read as 'draft'.

Item 1 asks which old spellings are read as a status. The pick maps only "in review" to review. So "under_review" and "LIVE" would not read as review and published, which is what the scenario expects. The run confirms that only in-review variants map and other non-enum values return null.

Item 3 asks what an unrecognised stored value reads as. The pick returns null, not a guessed nearest status, and the run shows "archived" giving null. Item 4 covers the empty and whitespace-only cases and also returns null, but item 3 is the closer match.

No item asks what is stored when a valid status is written. Item 5 is about whether near-miss input gets normalised, and its run only shows near-miss values throwing. It never shows writing "review" and getting "review" back.

Item 5 asks whether writing normalises near-miss input such as a different case, padding or an old spelling. The pick accepts only exact enum strings and throws for the rest, and the run shows "Draft", " draft" and "in-review" all throwing. Item 6 (the error message holds the quoted value) also agrees with the scenario's 'names the value' part.

Item 8 asks how unreadable values are reported in a batch read. The pick lists each original raw string once, de-duplicated by exact value and sorted, and the run shows this. That matches 'each distinct original value once, sorted, exactly as it was stored'.
